title: Wave 5 — si-jam-sessions — the signed lock's arithmetic, parser and callback, checked (P2): 13 recipes across 3 lanes
verifier_note: Seats: generators: Kimi k2.6 via Ollama Cloud (midi-notation-ingest, host-audio-and-midi); Grok 4.7 in a Cursor chat seat through scripts/seat_lane.py (integer-time, after Kimi returned no JSON in two rounds); verifier Claude Sonnet; compiler oracle sets 'jam' and 'jam-strict' (midly alloc + strict, new in this wave). Verifier: Claude Sonnet, one reasoning-stripped seat per lane (briefs/VERIFIER-BRIEF-W5.md): 9 confirmed, 4 corrected, 0 refuted, 0 unfindable. Compiler (non-model): rustc 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01) ran 19 checks, 0 failed. verified = ledger (external verdict AND compile gate).

lanes.title: The audio callback allocates nothing: proved on the callback body
lanes.verifier_note: Checked against rtrb 0.4.0 (src/lib.rs, arc_ring_buffer.rs, README.md), assert_no_alloc 1.1.2 (src/lib.rs, README.md) and the current GlobalAlloc/std::alloc docs, all retrieved at the pinned versions; every check in this lane was also re-run myself through compile_oracle.py (rustc 1.98.1, jam set, host target) rather than taken on trust, plus one counter-example of my own. All four matched their prose: recipe 1 printed alloc_count=0, recipe 2's negative control printed alloc_count>0 (proving the counting allocator is sensitive, not vacuous), recipe 3 printed new_allocates ops_do_not with RingBuffer::new confirmed to allocate twice (Vec::with_capacity + Box::new, via arc_ring_buffer.rs) while push/pop touch only atomics and raw pointers, and recipe 4's own check printed sum=10, confirming the non-allocating branch. The lane's one systemic weakness is in recipe 4: unlike the zero-allocation claims (recipes 1 and 3), which are backed by an explicit negative control (recipe 2) proving the measurement apparatus actually detects an allocation, the 'aborts if the callback body allocates' half of recipe 4's claim ships with no check that ever allocates inside the closure -- the provided check only exercises the return-normally path. I closed that gap myself with a counter-example (Vec::push inside assert_no_alloc with AllocDisabler registered), which aborted exactly as documented (exit 0xC0000409, stderr 'memory allocation of 8 bytes failed'), so the underlying claim holds, but the recipe's own verification story was incomplete without it.

recipes.name: Count allocations across a simulated audio callback popping rtrb into an f32 buffer
recipes.what: A counting #[global_allocator] records zero new allocations during a simulated callback that pops from an rtrb Consumer into a stack f32 buffer.
recipes.how: Implement GlobalAlloc by forwarding to System and incrementing an AtomicUsize in alloc. Create the RingBuffer and pre-fill events before resetting the counter. In the callback body, pop from the Consumer into a fixed [f32; N] on the stack. Compare the counter before and after; it must be identical.
recipes.gotchas: Do not measure RingBuffer::new itself; it allocates. Do not use Mutex or Vec inside the GlobalAlloc impl or measuring will recurse or allocate. Reset the counter after setup but before the callback body.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the signed lock pin: host audio callback must allocate nothing. Use this counting-allocator pattern to verify the callback body that pops committed events from an rtrb Consumer and writes them into the cpal output buffer.
recipes.verify_note: Ran the exact check via compile_oracle (rustc 1.98.1, jam set): printed alloc_count=0 as claimed. rtrb 0.4.0's pop()/push() (src/lib.rs) use only atomics and raw-pointer ops -- no alloc call sites exist.

checks.label: Counting allocator shows zero allocs in simulated callback body

recipes.name: Negative control: Vec push inside callback body increments allocator counter
recipes.what: A Vec::push inside the same simulated callback body increments the counting allocator, confirming the measurement is sensitive.
recipes.how: Use the same counting allocator. After resetting the counter, call vec.push(1.0) on a Vec::new() inside the simulated callback. Read the counter afterward; it is greater than zero.
recipes.gotchas: A Vec with reserved capacity may not allocate on push, so start with Vec::new(). The counting allocator must not itself allocate (e.g., no format! inside alloc).
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the signed lock pin: host audio callback must allocate nothing. This negative control demonstrates that the counting-allocator test is sensitive to allocations, ensuring a false negative is unlikely.
recipes.verify_note: Ran the exact check: Vec::new().push(1.0) printed alloc_count>0 -- the counting allocator is demonstrably sensitive, not a vacuous control. CountingAllocator itself only does an atomic add + System forwarding.

checks.label: Vec push inside callback body increments allocation counter

recipes.name: Create rtrb RingBuffer before the stream because only RingBuffer::new allocates
recipes.what: rtrb 0.4.0 allocates its backing buffer in RingBuffer::new, not during push or pop, so the ring must be created before the stream starts.
recipes.how: Call RingBuffer::new(capacity) during setup, before the cpal stream is built. Pass only the Producer to the non-real-time thread and the Consumer into the callback. Never construct or resize the ring inside the callback.
recipes.gotchas: RingBuffer::new may perform multiple backing allocations; the check only asserts the total is non-zero. Do not call new, grow, or shrink in the callback. The capacity is fixed and must be chosen at setup time.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the signed lock pin: host audio callback must allocate nothing. Because rtrb 0.4.0 only allocates in RingBuffer::new, the ring must be created before the cpal stream starts.
recipes.verify_note: Ran the exact check: printed 'new_allocates ops_do_not'. Source: RingBuffer::new does Vec::with_capacity + Box::new (2 allocs, confirmed via arc_ring_buffer.rs); push/pop touch only atomics/pointers.

checks.label: RingBuffer::new allocates but push and pop do not

recipes.name: Register assert_no_alloc AllocDisabler around the callback body to catch debug allocations
recipes.what: With AllocDisabler registered as #[global_allocator], assert_no_alloc aborts in debug if the callback body allocates and returns normally when it does not.
recipes.how: Add assert_no_alloc as a dependency, register #[global_allocator] static A: AllocDisabler = AllocDisabler;, and wrap the callback body in assert_no_alloc(move || { ... }). In debug builds, any allocation inside the closure triggers an abort via handle_alloc_error.
recipes.gotchas: Default features disable the guard in release; for debug-only protection this is correct. The closure must not drop heap-allocated types that deallocate inside the forbidden zone unless wrapped in PermitDrop. The oracle has no audio device, so this only proves the callback body, not cpal's backend thread.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the signed lock pin: host audio callback must allocate nothing. Use assert_no_alloc as a second, independent guard around the callback body in debug builds.
recipes.verify_note: The check only proves the no-alloc branch (sum=10). My own counter-example (alloc inside the closure) aborted: exit 0xC0000409, stderr 'memory allocation of 8 bytes failed' -- confirms the untested abort half.

corrections.claim: Recipe's own check exercises only the non-allocating path (sum=10). The 'aborts if it allocates' half is real -- confirmed by AllocDisabler::check()'s handle_alloc_error call and by my own compiled counter-example, which aborted -- but no check here exercises it.

checks.label: assert_no_alloc returns normally when callback body does not allocate

lanes.title: PPQ 3360 and the u128 tick-to-sample rule, checked
lanes.verifier_note: Checked against: rustc 1.98.1 stable docs (u128 checked_mul/div/rem, Cargo overflow-checks, operator-expr overflow, the wasm32-unknown-unknown platform page), all retrieved live via WebFetch; midly 0.5.3 src/primitive.rs read from the local cargo registry and cross-checked live on docs.rs (byte-identical: u15/u24 masks, Timing::Metrical doc comments); the signed si-jam-sessions Phase 0 lock fetched at its pinned commit e3cc85e via the GitHub API for every engine_note; the compile oracle run over the whole lane (6/6 checks PASS, exact stdout); and independent Python bigint recomputation of every numeric claim in recipes 1-4 (all 8 tuplet levels at 4 PPQs, the u128 overflow bound and its 2.44e19-day floor, the carried-remainder equality at 4 PPQs), plus one original counter-example (tick=tempo=1e15, ppq=1) proving recipe 5s u64-quotient-overflow refusal path is real and distinct from its tested ppq=0 path, with no panic. Nothing failed; all five are confirmed and solid, and PHASE-0.md explicitly cites two of these five findings (PPQ 3360s tuplet-exactness, the tick-to-sample formula) as already verified by this KB. Systemic weakness: every check in this lane is self-referential -- the same Rust program both derives and asserts its numbers, so a shared conceptual error in the generators arithmetic would compile and pass silently; the only real guard is a verifier reimplementing the arithmetic independently, which is what this pass did in Python rather than re-trusting the compilers rerun of the same code. A second, smaller weakness: 4 of 5 recipes lean on one page (doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/primitive.u128.html) for their core API warrant, so that single page is a concentration point for the whole lanes Rust-currency claim.

recipes.name: Print whole-tick 3:2, 5:4 and 7:4 durations from a whole note through a 128th at PPQ 3360
recipes.what: At PPQ 3360 every 3:2, 5:4 and 7:4 tuplet of a whole, half, quarter, eighth, sixteenth, thirty-second, sixty-fourth and hundred-twenty-eighth note is a whole number of ticks.
recipes.how: PPQ 3360 = 32*3*5*7. Note ticks for level k in 0..=7 are 3360*4/2^k (whole down to a 128th). One tuplet note is note*2/3, note*4/5 or note*4/7. Require checked_rem of that numerator to be 0 and keep the checked_div quotient: the 128th is 70, 84 and 60.
recipes.rust_version: 1.98.1, edition 2024; SMF ticks/beat is midly 0.5.3 u15
recipes.gotchas: A 7:8 septuplet is a different ratio and is not what this grid was factored for. PPQ 960 and 3840 still have no factor of 7, so switching the written ratio to another power of two does not make those 7-tuplets whole ticks. Do not round an f64 tuplet back onto this grid.
recipes.engine_note: Signed lock: the score is integer ticks at PPQ 3360 (2^5 * 3 * 5 * 7), with no floating point in the time path. Store that PPQ in Timing::Metrical and use these whole-tick 3:2, 5:4 and 7:4 lengths for onset and duration.
recipes.verify_note: Recomputed all 8 note-levels x3 ratios in Python at PPQ 3360=2^5*3*5*7: exact match to stdout/how (128th=70/84/60). midly src confirms Timing::Metrical(u15). Oracle PASS. Lock@e3cc85e cites this exact rationale.

recipes.name: Show every 7:4 tuplet from a whole note through a 128th is not a whole tick at PPQ 480, 960 and 3840
recipes.what: At PPQ 480, 960 and 3840 the 3:2 and 5:4 tuplets of those eight note values are whole ticks, and every 7:4 tuplet of them is not.
recipes.how: Use the same note ticks PPQ*4/2^k and the same ratios 2/3, 4/5 and 4/7. Count checked_rem == 0. Each of 480, 960 and 3840 yields 8, 8 and 0. All three PPQs, and 3360, are <= the u15 mask (1 << 15) - 1.
recipes.rust_version: 1.98.1, edition 2024; SMF ticks/beat is midly 0.5.3 u15
recipes.gotchas: 480, 960 and 3840 are common MIDI divisions and they do represent straight 128ths, because each is divisible by 32. They fail only the factor of 7. Fitting in the 15-bit header field is not the same as representing a septuplet.
recipes.engine_note: Signed lock: integer ticks at PPQ 3360 and no f64 in the time path. Do not adopt PPQ 480, 960 or 3840 for the law; every 7:4 from a whole through a 128th is a fractional tick there. Refuse a metrical header whose PPQ is not 3360.
recipes.verify_note: Recomputed t3/t5/t7 counts for PPQ 480/960/3840 in Python: (8,8,0) each, all eight 7:4 fail -- exact match to stdout. u15 mask 32767 >= all 4 PPQs (checked). Oracle PASS. Engine_note matches locks single fixed PPQ 3360.

sources.title: u128 checked_rem
sources.claim: u128::checked_rem computes self % rhs and returns None if rhs is 0, so a remainder of Some(0) is an exact division.

recipes.name: Bound the largest tick whose product with 16777215 and 48000 still fits in u128
recipes.what: tick.checked_mul(16777215).and_then(|p| p.checked_mul(48000)) is Some for every tick through 422550225262032543670307476 and None at the next tick; at PPQ 3360 that bound is a floor of 24419973467535932409 days.
recipes.how: Tempo is (1 << 24) - 1, which equals 0xFFFFFF. factor = tempo.checked_mul(48000). max_tick = u128::MAX.checked_div(factor). Require max_tick.checked_mul(factor) to be Some and (max_tick + 1).checked_mul(factor) to be None. Floor days are max_tick * tempo / 3360 / 1_000_000 / 86_400. The same factor times u64::MAX is still Some.
recipes.gotchas: A bare * panics on overflow only when overflow-checks is enabled, and wraps when it is disabled. checked_mul returns None in either build. u64::MAX cannot reach this bound, but the sample quotient of a huge tick can still exceed u64, so the export must refuse when the quotient does not fit in the 64-bit return.
recipes.engine_note: Signed lock: tick to sample is computed in u128 with checked_* and a refusal on None, and the release profile sets overflow-checks = true. Keep the product tick * tempo_us_per_quarter * 48000 on checked_mul; a musical take ends long before tick 422550225262032543670307476.
recipes.verify_note: Independent Python bigint recompute: factor=805306320000, max_tick=422550225262032543670307476, overflows at +1, u64::MAX*factor fits, days=24419973467535932409 -- all exact. WebFetch confirmed checked_mul + overflow-checks docs.

checks.label: checked_mul fits the max tick times 16777215 times 48000 and refuses the next tick

recipes.name: Match one floor of a multi-segment span by carrying the remainder while independent floors drift
recipes.what: Flooring each tempo segment with the remainder of tick * tempo_us * 48000 divided by PPQ * 10^6 carried forward equals one floor of the summed numerators, and summing the separate floors is one sample lower for two one-tick segments at tempo 16777215 on PPQ 3360, 480, 960 and 3840.
recipes.how: denom = ppq.checked_mul(1_000_000). numer = ticks.checked_mul(tempo).checked_mul(48000).checked_add(rem). The segment returns (numer.checked_div(denom), numer.checked_rem(denom)) and the next segment adds that remainder before dividing. For ticks = 1 and tempo = (1 << 24) - 1 the carried totals are 479, 3355, 1677 and 419; the independent sums are 478, 3354, 1676 and 418.
recipes.gotchas: Cancelling 48000/10^6 down to 6/125 before the carry changes the modulus, so a remainder from the reduced fraction is not the remainder the next segment must add. Summing floor(segment) drops a sample whenever successive remainders add up to at least one denominator.
recipes.engine_note: Signed lock: tick to sample = floor(tick * tempo_us_per_quarter * 48000 / (PPQ * 10^6)) in u128, with the remainder carried across tempo segments, checked_* and a refusal on None. Carry this unreduced remainder; do not add independent per-segment floors.
recipes.verify_note: Independent Python bigint recompute at PPQ 3360/480/960/3840: carried 479/3355/1677/419 vs independent 478/3354/1676/418, carried==floor(sum) every time -- exact match to prose+stdout. Own scenario also confirms r2<denom.

recipes.name: Export the u128 tick-to-sample floor from a wasm32 cdylib that takes and returns u64
recipes.what: wasm32-unknown-unknown can export tick_to_sample(tick: u64, tempo_us_per_quarter: u64, ppq: u64) -> u64, which floors tick * tempo * 48000 / (ppq * 10^6) in u128 and returns 48000 for one quarter at 1000000 microseconds and PPQ 3360; tick_to_sample_status returns 1 when checked_div refuses a zero PPQ.
recipes.how: Build an edition 2024 cdylib with #[unsafe(no_mangle)] extern "C" functions. Widen each u64 to u128, then checked_mul by the tempo, checked_mul by 48000, checked_div by ppq.checked_mul(1_000_000), and u64::try_from the quotient. tick_to_sample returns the quotient or u64::MAX on None; tick_to_sample_status returns 0 or 1. Call them from node with BigInt arguments.
recipes.gotchas: println! does nothing on wasm32-unknown-unknown, so the sample has to be the export's return value. A JS number is not an i64 argument; node must pass a BigInt. u64::MAX as the refusal sentinel collides with a genuine quotient of 2^64-1, which is why the status export is the refusal signal.
recipes.engine_note: Signed lock: edition 2024 cdylib for wasm32-unknown-unknown, raw extern "C" with #[unsafe(no_mangle)], every export argument and return at most 64 bits, status codes across the boundary and no panic. Compute the floor in u128 inside the export and return status 1 on None.
recipes.verify_note: Both wasm_call checks PASS (compiler-executed, BigInt args). Hand-verified 3360*1e6*48000/(3360*1e6)=48000. Own counter-example (tick=tempo=1e15,ppq=1) proves the u64-quotient-overflow refusal is real and distinct from ppq=0, no panic.

checks.label: wasm32 tick_to_sample(3360, 1000000, 3360) returns 48000
wasm32 tick_to_sample_status returns 1 when PPQ is 0

lanes.title: midly with strict: what the law's parser rejects, compiled
lanes.verifier_note: Checked all 4 recipes against midly 0.5.3's own source (src/smf.rs, error.rs, event.rs, primitive.rs, lib.rs, riff.rs), read both from the local cargo registry and freshly via WebFetch against every cited docs.rs source URL (5 unique URLs, all resolved, all midly 0.5.3, all byte-identical to the local copy). Re-ran all 9 given checks through compile_oracle.py under the jam and jam-strict oracle sets (9/9 pass originally); cross-checked every engine_note against the signed lock quoted in VERIFIER-BRIEF-W5.md, independently reconfirmed against the live docs/PHASE-0.md on GitHub. RE-ADJUDICATED export-smpte-refusal-and-error-kind-mapping-from-wasm32-strict-cdylib on coordinator-relayed evidence: reproduced myself that Timing::read (primitive.rs:495, `-(bit_range!(raw,8..16) as i8)`) negates i8::MIN and panics when the header's division high byte is exactly 0x80, under both strict and non-strict alike (Timing::read has no strict gate) - host exit 101 'attempt to negate with overflow'; the recipe's own wasm ingest() pattern does not trap on this input either, it hangs indefinitely (my wasm_call timed out at 20s, no return, no RuntimeError), worse than 'without panicking' implies. Also independently confirmed the boundary bytes: 0x81->Err(Invalid), 0xE8/E7/E3/E2->Fps24/25/29/30 - the defect is the single byte value 0x80. Separately confirmed (smf.rs, riff.rs) that strict gates neither the unknown-top-level-chunk skip (Chunk::read's `_=>()` arm) nor riff::unwrap's RMID-only/data-chunk-only RIFF handling - both unconditional in both modes - but none of this lane's other 3 recipes or their engine_notes claim otherwise, so no other verdict changed on that point. Original, still-standing finding on the other two: on the non-strict ('jam') side, 2 of 4 recipes' 'how' prose claims a specific permissive outcome (an empty resulting track after silent truncation; 0xFF masked to exactly 0x0F) that the paired check only asserts as bare res.is_ok(), never the specific value - I closed both gaps myself with independent oracle runs (tracks[0].len()==0; channel.as_int()==15) and confirmed both claims true, so those two stayed corrected rather than refuted.

recipes.name: Reject track-count mismatch under midly strict
recipes.what: midly 0.5.3 strict rejects an SMF whose header track-count hint does not match the number of MTrk chunks, while alloc-only accepts it.
recipes.how: Build an SMF with header format Parallel, track count 2, but supply only one EndOfTrack track. Parse with Smf::parse. Under jam the result is Ok; under jam-strict validate_smf returns ErrorKind::Malformed("file has a different amount of tracks than declared").
recipes.gotchas: Without strict, midly silently ignores the mismatch and returns the tracks it found. Do not assume header counts are validated unless strict is enabled.
recipes.engine_note: Signed lock (si-jam-sessions docs/PHASE-0.md @ e3cc85e): midly 0.5.3 is built with default-features = false, features = ["alloc", "strict"]. Use Smf::parse in the ingest path; any Malformed error from strict mode must be mapped to a refusal code and returned across the wasm boundary, never panicked.
recipes.verify_note: validate_smf's message matches smf.rs verbatim. Oracle ran both checks: jam->Ok, jam-strict->Malformed with the exact quoted string. Confirmed live on docs.rs 0.5.3, byte-identical to the local registry copy.

checks.label: alloc-only accepts track-count mismatch
strict rejects track-count mismatch
stdout_contains: file has a different amount of tracks than declared

recipes.name: Reject truncated MTrk chunk under midly strict
recipes.what: midly 0.5.3 strict rejects an SMF whose MTrk chunk length exceeds the remaining file bytes, while alloc-only silently uses the remainder.
recipes.how: Build a single-track SMF with an MTrk header declaring length 16 but only 2 bytes of data following. Under jam, Chunk::read uses the remainder and Smf::parse returns Ok with an empty track. Under jam-strict, Chunk::read returns err_malformed and Smf::parse fails.
recipes.gotchas: Non-strict silently truncates the chunk and may return an empty track or partial events. This hides file corruption.
recipes.engine_note: Signed lock (si-jam-sessions docs/PHASE-0.md @ e3cc85e): midly 0.5.3 strict must reject truncated chunks. Map the resulting Malformed error to a refusal status code in the wasm export.
recipes.verify_note: Chunk::read (smf.rs) bails 'reached eof before chunk ended' under strict; TrackIter::next() re-wraps it as 'invalid chunk', which check 1 tests. I independently confirmed the non-strict path yields tracks=1, track0 len=0.

corrections.claim: Check 0 only asserts res.is_ok(), not the 'how' claim of an empty resulting track. Verified independently: parsing these bytes under jam gives tracks=1, tracks[0].len()=0 - claim holds, but the check wouldn't catch a regression that kept partial events.

recipes.name: Reject out-of-range MidiChannel meta-event under midly strict
recipes.what: midly 0.5.3 strict rejects a MidiChannel meta-event (type 0x20) whose data byte exceeds 0x0F, while alloc-only masks it to a valid u4.
recipes.how: Construct a single-track SMF containing the track event FF 20 01 FF. Under jam, u4::read masks 0xFF to 0x0F and Smf::parse returns Ok. Under jam-strict, u4::try_from fails and Smf::parse returns ErrorKind::Malformed.
recipes.gotchas: Without strict, midly applies a lossy mask to restricted integers. A parse success does not mean the file is standards-compliant.
recipes.engine_note: Signed lock (si-jam-sessions docs/PHASE-0.md @ e3cc85e): midly 0.5.3 strict must reject out-of-range integers. Map the resulting Malformed error to a refusal status code in the wasm export.
recipes.verify_note: event.rs: MidiChannel reads via u4::read, confirmed verbatim. primitive.rs int_feature 'read' arm: strict uses try_from->Malformed. Check 1 confirms 'malformed event' after two context wraps; I confirmed non-strict masks 0xFF->15.

corrections.claim: Check 0 only asserts res.is_ok(), not the 'how' claim that 0xFF masks to 0x0F. Verified independently: channel.as_int()==15 under jam - claim holds, but the check wouldn't catch a regression that stored a different masked channel value.

strict rejects MidiChannel 0xFF as Malformed

sources.claim: The int_feature macro implements IntRead::read for restricted integers so that under strict, try_from is used and returns ErrorKind::Malformed if the raw value exceeds the allowed mask.

recipes.name: Export SMPTE refusal and error-kind mapping from wasm32 strict cdylib
recipes.what: midly 0.5.3 strict compiles and runs in a wasm32-unknown-unknown cdylib; a raw extern "C" export reads SMF bytes and returns 0 for Ok, 1 for Invalid, 2 for Malformed, and 3 for SMPTE Timecode timing, without panicking.
recipes.how: Write a #![no_std] cdylib with a bump allocator and panic handler. Expose #[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn ingest() -> u64. Match Smf::parse result: Ok with Timing::Timecode => 3, Ok otherwise => 0, Err with Invalid => 1, Err with Malformed => 2.
recipes.gotchas: wasm32-unknown-unknown has no default allocator; you must supply a #[global_allocator] and a #[panic_handler]. Keep the export panic-free and return only u64.
recipes.engine_note: Signed lock (si-jam-sessions docs/PHASE-0.md @ e3cc85e): the wasm32 cdylib export must parse SMF bytes with midly strict and return a u64 status code. SMPTE-timed files are refused with status 3. ErrorKind::Invalid maps to 1 and ErrorKind::Malformed maps to 2.
recipes.verify_note: Reproduced independently: byte 0x80 in the division field makes Timing::read (primitive.rs:495) negate i8::MIN and panic, in both strict and non-strict. The wasm ingest() export doesn't trap on it either - it hangs (20s timeout, no return).

corrections.claim: FALSE AS WRITTEN: division high byte 0x80 makes Timing::read negate i8::MIN, panicking (primitive.rs:495) in strict and non-strict alike; the recipe's own wasm export hangs, not returns 1/2/3. Fix: inspect the raw division word's bit 15 and refuse as status 3 before calling Smf::parse.

wasm strict export returns 2 for Malformed
wasm strict export returns 3 for SMPTE timing
